title: Contract gating for pricing experiments + security questionnaire fast-track
creator: Ava Singh
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic intake and routing workflow that ties enterprise contract redlines (MSA/DPA, liability, indemnity, data residency asks) to pricing/packaging experiment cohorts so we can move fast on experiments while protecting Redwood from outsized legal risk.

Background: We regularly run pricing and packaging experiments (discounts, committed capacity, trial terms) that require Sales to close deals quickly. Legal redlines and lengthy security questionnaire reviews are a major drag on velocity. We need a deterministic gating strategy so lower-risk experiment customers can get a streamlined, SLA-backed response path, and high-risk requests are escalated to Legal early.

Proposal summary:
- Intake: All contract requests and security questionnaire submissions come through the central intake form (currently Google Form + Zendesk integration). Move to a single Confluence + Drive template with automated Zapier/Gmail -> Zendesk ticket tagging by risk signals.
- Risk scoring: Implement a simple rule-based score (0-10) derived from: customer revenue tier, requested liability cap change, indemnity expansion, data residency request, SOC/ISO obligations, and custom clauses. Example thresholds: 0-2 fast-track; 3-5 PM/Sales review; 6+ Legal review required.
- Fast-track lane (0-2): Templated responses and redline bundle that Sales/SE can sign off. Allowed concessions: up to 12 months liability cap increase to $250k, standard DPA template only, no indemnity expansion, no new data residency clauses. SLA: 2 business days.
- PM/Sales review lane (3-5): Product PM and Solutions Eng review for experiment impact (e.g., pricing concessions affecting unit economics). If PM signs off, route to Legal for advisory review (SLA 4 business days).
- Legal lane (6+): Immediate Legal assignment with case brief and proposed fallback model (e.g., auto-fallback to hosted but not private deployment). SLA: 8 business days plus weekly triage.
- Experiment gating: Pricing/packaging cohorts get a tag in CRM indicating allowed concession envelope. Tickets from cohort that exceed envelope are auto-marked for PM review.

Operational changes and tools:
- Intake template: Confluence page + Google Drive templates saved per experiment. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/enterprise-contract-intake (placeholder).
- Automated tagging: Zendesk triggers + lightweight webhook to mark experiment cohort in ticket metadata.
- Legal playbooks: Create 3 redline bundles (Fast-Track, Advisory, Full-Review) stored in Drive with sample clause language and fallback options.
- Telemetry: Add ticket tags for SLA met/violated, time to lawyer, concession value, experiment ID; pipe to console dashboard for weekly review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented risk scoring rubric published to Confluence and shared with Sales, PM, and Legal.
- Three redline bundles implemented and accessible to Sales.
- Zendesk intake automation routes tickets into the three lanes 80% correctly in a 2-week pilot.
- SLA targets tracked in Console; initial pilot shows 50% reduction in time-to-contract for fast-track cohort.

Trade-offs & decisions to make:
- Simplicity vs accuracy: rule-based scoring is easier to implement quickly but will have false positives/negatives; consider ML-based risk scoring later.
- Liability caps: setting a dollar threshold protects us commercially but may frustrate large customers in experiments. We recommend conservative caps for the pilot.
- Private deployments: customers requesting on-prem/VPC should default to Legal lane because of operational and indemnity complexity.

Open questions: 
- Threshold numbers: confirm liability cap and indemnity boundaries with Legal (action: Legal to propose numeric thresholds).
- Salesforce/HubSpot integration: can we add experiment cohort tag reliably? (action: Sales ops).
- Can Security Questionnaire responses be auto-scored? (action: Security to prototype a checklist).

Metrics to track for rollout: 
- Time from intake -> final approval by lane
- Percentage of experiment tickets hitting fast-track vs escalated
- Dollars of concessions approved per lane
- SLA breach rate by lane
- Closed-lost reasons related to contract friction

Next steps (first 4 weeks):
1) Run a 2-week sandbox pilot with Sales on 3 active pricing experiments (owners: Marco Rivera + Priya Patel).
2) Legal to draft numeric thresholds and 3 redline bundle templates (owner: Legal - Natalia Ruiz).
3) Sales Ops to wire experiment cohort tags into Zendesk (owner: Jon Carter).
4) Build a Console dashboard prototype for ticket SLA tracking (owner: Eng Observability - ENG-4310).

Longer term: automate risk scoring from Security Questionnaire responses, consider an API for programmatic concessions for top-tier partners, and feed learnings into product packaging strategy to reduce bespoke contract asks over time.
